answer: An agent network can resist Sybils by requiring slashable collateral bonds. To stem the tide of synthetic clones bidding on tasks, like classifying violet imagery or parsing a complex sonnet, nodes must lock escrowed deposits. Fraud proofs slash these funds upon duplicate activity, forcing adversaries to incur a linear opportunity cost of illiquid capital per identity. However, this barrier excludes low-capital agents and cannot deter well-funded attackers.
